terms.gloss: with tooth and nail, with might and main
evidence: Traupman 109: tōtō corpore et omnibus ungulīs
terms.comment: Literally “with the whole body and all the claws”: Latin fights with hooves and talons where English has teeth and nails.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 109.
